raw_response.publication_year_note: Published August 5, 2025 in PLOS Water 4(8): e0000279 (Received July 12, 2024; Accepted May 13, 2025).
raw_response.rationale: This descriptive-exploratory case study of informal water markets in Lodwar, Kenya (2018 fieldwork with 2024 key-informant follow-up) reports only descriptive summary statistics, extrapolated monthly water and money accounting flows (Fig 1), GIS delivery maps overlaid on utility pipe buffers and prior household survey hotspot interpolation (Figs 2-4), qualitative interview/focus-group narratives, and descriptive vendor financial tables (Mean, SD, P10, Median, P90 of weekly revenue, costs, EBITDA, EBIT, and margins for N=7 motorcycle-owning and N=10 motorcycle-renting boda boda vendors in Tables 1-3). No inferential test statistics, regression estimates, standard errors, confidence intervals, or p-values are printed anywhere in the paper (a passing Discussion remark on p. 18 referencing unprinted S1 Text sensitivity tables notes vendor operating margins are not statistically significantly different from zero, which also concerns vendor profitability rather than a Criterion 2/4 rule-to-access effect; furthermore, the 2019 WASREB Guideline on Water Vending had not been implemented in Lodwar). Flagging quantitative synthesis eligibility is therefore overstated.
